findings.finding: Monitoring suppression is structural, not merely uncertain coexistence. CPython instrumentation suppresses event delivery while executing an instrumentation callback; legacy sys.setprofile is implemented through those callbacks. Python audit hooks similarly enter tracing unless explicitly traceable. The original hook has no such attribute.

Actual audit/copy_begin/copy_finish calls are invisible, while canonical/read/provenance/ancestry/hash helpers have mixed visible and suppressed callers. Entire missed invocations generate neither start nor return/unwind, so an empty balanced29-target stack cannot prove coverage. Existing copy histories can expose missing counts, but make the proposed all-call coverage gate fail rather than recover the missing durations.

directory_profile is absent from29targets and adding its code would not solve callback suppression. Its copy_metadata_profile and directory_profile_event work, including SHA verification, is also unobserved directly. Visible product/guard parent intervals still include that work; ranking their exclusive_target_cpu as product/guard self cost misattributes hidden observers.

process_time_ns measures all process threads. Invalidating only foreign selected-code events cannot exclude CPU in unselected worker code. Use thread CPU for main-thread attribution and retain total process CPU separately; no zeroing of unobserved worker contribution.

Default audit may recursively invoke audit on frame-code access; audit inside directory_profile overlaps its enclosing profile interval. Direct inline timers must count outer audit separately and record its profile overlap. Never sum overlapping inclusive totals, either between these callbacks or against monitored parent targets.

Monitoring callbacks and their timer callees execute while tracing is suppressed; the earlier proposal statement that these timer calls may themselves be seen by the original global profile is not supported on the exact source. Their overhead remains real but is not recursively profiled.

Inline finally is not a completion receipt for deny/_exit or kill. Latest cumulative metrics describe only completed intervals through the saved boundary. C dispatch, collector cost, startup outside activation, final unsaved work and open intervals remain explicit residual/UNKNOWN.

Provided inline source diff preserves original callback bodies and other original top-level AST nodes. New source bytes/line layouts require fresh pins and exact source-control qualification; no legacy evidence transfer and no claim of runtime guard equivalence from AST alone.
